subject: Workplace Skills
title: Checklists Prevent Failure
description: Learn Checklists Prevent Failure in one minute.

hook.text: Surgeon Atul Gawande found that a simple 19-item checklist reduced surgical complications by 36%.

buildup.text: Checklists work because human memory is unreliable under pressure. Even experts skip steps routinely.

discovery.text: A checklist externalizes critical steps. It frees your mind for judgment instead of consuming it on recall.

twist.text: Pilots, surgeons, and engineers all use checklists. Knowledge workers resist them, losing quality without knowing.

climax.text: Create a checklist for any repeated process. Keep it short — five to nine items is the ideal range.

punchline.text: Checklists aren't beneath experts. They free them.

quiz.question: Why do checklists improve performance even for experts?
options: They slow down the process to reduce errors
They externalize steps so the mind can focus on judgment
They require less training to follow
